title: Tech and Security Companies Respond to PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities
content_md: Tech vendors, cybersecurity companies and government agencies have published advisories, detections and mitigations for the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, while many software makers are still checking whether their own products are exposed. The two critical bugs , CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, can let unauthenticated attackers execute code remotely. Wiz, OpenAI and Calif identified them in August, and PHP addressed them on October 21 with versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. PHP pushed out the release one day ahead of the planned disclosure, after the CVE identifiers started circulating online on October 20. Amazon says the first exploitation attempt came on October 17, before the embargo lifted. Hadrian, Patchstack and Cloudflare all detected attack attempts in the hours leading up to the patches. WatchTowr saw mass exploitation soon after the fixes were published, although the PoC exploits in circulation did not achieve code execution. With PHP built into a wide range of commercial software, appliances and cloud services, companies across the industry have had to check their exposure. Tech vendors check products, update PHP runtimes Cisco’s advisory names over 30 products and cloud services under review. Among them are Identity Services Engine, Catalyst Center, Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, Expressway, Umbrella, Webex and the AppDynamics PHP Agent. “Currently, no products are known to be affected,” Cisco says.
